<!-- GENERATED by tools/docs_gen.py. Do not edit; run `make docs-gen`. -->

24 commands (schema v1). Agents: run `gigai agent-context --json` for the machine-readable form.

- **effect**: `read` never changes state; `write` may change GigAI state or files (for some commands only with certain options).
- **external**: the strongest thing the command can reach. `none` is offline, `model` may call a model provider (cost, and text leaves this machine), `network` may make other network requests.

## `gigai scout answer`

Answer one interview question once; the answer is reused across every posting.

`gigai scout answer [OPTIONS] QUESTION_ID`

effect: `write` · external: `model` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout answer q-visa --answer-text "I need H-1B sponsorship"
gigai scout answer cloud:gcp --question "Have you run workloads on GCP?" --answer-text "Yes: two years of batch workloads." --profile profile_1 --json
```

The answer goes into one profile's story bank (--profile; default: the profile the --reassess job was assessed for, else the selected profile) and is reused by that profile's later assessments, also when a posting words the question differently. --question keeps the question's own words with it; --actor agent records that an agent wrote it. An answer holding an email, phone, link, street address or the saved name is refused (personal_info_refused). --reassess JOB_URL_OR_ID re-runs the assessment with a model (external=model).

## `gigai scout assess`

Assess ONE job against a resume right now, without a find-jobs run.

`gigai scout assess [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `model` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout assess --job-url https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1 --resume resume.md --json
```

Calls the configured model adapter (default from find-jobs.json). --job-url may fetch the posting over the network.

## `gigai scout discover`

Run the weekly company-discovery engine (OpenAI web_search + H-1B baseline).

`gigai scout discover [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `network` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout discover --runs 3
```

Foreground; can take 5-30 minutes. Calls OpenAI web_search (network + model) and needs credentials. --status only reads.

## `gigai scout install`

Bind, approve, and activate Scout for the bound project; safe to rerun.

`gigai scout install [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object, including "stopped_server" (always null for install).

Example:

```sh
gigai scout install
```

## `gigai scout profile list`

List the profiles and what each one searches with.

`gigai scout profile list [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout profile list --json
```

The default profile uses the setup settings (location, work mode, countries, posted window); every other profile has its own, or the default's when it has none. The first read of a project stores its default profile.

## `gigai scout profile update`

Set a profile's own location, work mode, countries and posted window.

`gigai scout profile update [OPTIONS] PROFILE_ID`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout profile update profile_1 --location "Houston, TX" --work-mode hybrid --country US --max-age-days 30
gigai scout profile update profile_1 --same-as-default
```

Only the options given change; no other profile is changed. The default profile is refused: it uses the setup settings (Settings in the Scout UI). The location is a search setting, not the resume's contact line.

## `gigai scout resume add`

Import a file as the resume reference and create the record find-jobs reads.

`gigai scout resume add [OPTIONS] FILE`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume add resume.md
```

Works as the very first command on a fresh machine: writes the default GigAI settings (like 'gigai scout run'), installs Scout if needed, then imports the file. Never rewrites an existing config.

## `gigai scout resume pdf`

Render a resume to PDF locally: your own markdown, or a stored tailored resume.

`gigai scout resume pdf [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, out_path, source, pages, bytes, spacing_scale}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume pdf --in resume.md --out resume.pdf --json
gigai scout resume pdf --in resume.md --out resume.pdf --profile profile_1 --spacing 0.9
gigai scout resume pdf --tailored --job-url https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1 --out acme.pdf --json
```

No model call and no network: the markdown is only rendered, never stored. --in takes resume markdown in GigAI's format (## Summary, ## Experience with ### entries and - bullets, ## Skills, ## Education, ## Projects, ## Other; trailing <!-- ... --> comments are dropped), so the markdown of a tailored resume renders as it is. The PDF header (name, title, contact line) always comes from the saved Resume display settings, never from the markdown. --spacing (0.7-1.4) and --auto-fit/--no-auto-fit change the layout for this render only; --spacing alone turns auto fit off. Writes only --out. To change two bullets and render: edit the two lines in the markdown file and run the first example; for a stored tailored resume, change the lines with PUT /api/tailored-resumes/lines (use: custom) and run the --tailored example.

## `gigai scout resume tailor`

Tailor a resume to ONE job posting right now: markdown, every line sourced.

`gigai scout resume tailor [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `model` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume tailor --job-url https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1 --resume resume.md --out tailored.md
```

Calls the configured model adapter; name and contact lines are removed before the model sees the resume text. --job-url may fetch the posting.

## `gigai scout run`

Install/activate Scout if needed, then start (or reuse) its local API + UI.

`gigai scout run [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object, including "stopped_server": {pid, home, target} for a verified older Scout server that was stopped to free the port, else null.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout run --no-browser
```

Serves on localhost only. Once running, GET /api describes the HTTP API.

## `gigai scout snapshot export`

Write a metadata-only snapshot of the stored company index (postings, title tags, board validators) and print the gh commands to publish it.

`gigai scout snapshot export [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout snapshot export --out ./snapshot
gigai scout snapshot export --out ./snapshot-next --base ./snapshot/manifest.json
```

No descriptions and no private paths are written (scanned before success); every file is re-opened and its SHA-256 checked. With --base, a delta file and a removal list of boards and postings that are gone are added. Never publishes: the gh commands are printed as text for you to run.

## `gigai scout snapshot import`

Download the published metadata snapshot (postings, title tags, board validators; no descriptions) and add it to the stored company index.

`gigai scout snapshot import [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `network` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout snapshot import
gigai scout snapshot import --from ./snapshot
```

Takes the full files, or only the delta when the stored snapshot is the delta's base. Every file's SHA-256 is checked before it is read. A board checked on this machine at or after the snapshot is left alone, and nothing local is deleted except boards the snapshot itself added and later lists as removed. Unreachable or not published is a quiet no-op (exit 0); a snapshot that fails its checks or cannot be written exits 1 with the stored postings unchanged. Makes no request when the snapshot.enabled setting (or GIGAI_SCOUT_SNAPSHOT=0) turns it off.

`gigai scout snapshot status [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout snapshot status
```

## `gigai scout sources update`

Check every company board on the watchlist and store what changed.

`gigai scout sources update [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `network` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh

```

One conditional request per board (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby). Resumable if the time budget stops it.

`gigai scout stop [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.


## `gigai scout story-bank add`

Add a new story bank entry: a story, or an answer nobody asked for yet.

`gigai scout story-bank add [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, profile_id, entry}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout story-bank add --question "Tell me about a database migration you led" --answer-file story.md --actor agent --json
gigai scout story-bank add --question "Kafka?" --answer-text "Three years running Kafka in production." --id tool:kafka --tag streaming
```

Local, no model call. The entry's id is --id, or story:<the question's first words>. A later assessment of this profile is offered a one-line summary of the entry and reuses it for a requirement it covers instead of asking. story_exists (with the current entry in --json) when the profile already has that id: use edit. Text holding an email, phone, link, street address or the saved name is refused (personal_info_refused).

## `gigai scout story-bank delete`

Remove one of the profile's own story bank entries.

`gigai scout story-bank delete [OPTIONS] QUESTION_ID`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, profile_id, deleted}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout story-bank delete cloud:gcp --confirm --json
gigai scout story-bank delete cloud:gcp --confirm --updated-at 2026-10-01T15:00:00.000000Z --json
```

Needs --confirm. The entry is never listed, offered or sent to a model again; the project's journal keeps the older revision of the record it was in. With --updated-at (the value you read) the delete is refused with story_bank_changed when the entry changed since.

## `gigai scout story-bank edit`

Edit one of the profile's own story bank entries: the answer, the question words and/or the tag.

`gigai scout story-bank edit [OPTIONS] QUESTION_ID`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, profile_id, entry}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout story-bank edit cloud:gcp --answer-text "Yes: three years of batch and streaming workloads on GCP." --json
gigai scout story-bank edit cloud:gcp --tag "cloud platforms" --actor agent --updated-at 2026-10-01T15:00:00.000000Z --json
```

A new answer is a new revision of the stored answer; every write bumps the entry's revision and updated_at and records who wrote it (--actor). Pass --updated-at (the updated_at you read with show --json) to be safe against a concurrent write: when the entry changed since, the edit is refused with story_bank_changed and --json carries the current entry. An empty --tag puts the automatic tag back. A shared entry is edited in the profile that owns it.

## `gigai scout story-bank list`

List a profile's story bank: every answered question and story, with its tag and the jobs that used it.

`gigai scout story-bank list [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, profile_id, entries, total, tags, sharing}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout story-bank list --json
gigai scout story-bank list --profile profile_1 --search kubernetes --tag technical --json
```

The profile's own entries, then (shared: true) those of the one profile it is set to share with. A profile never lists another profile's answers otherwise. Each entry carries question_id, question, answer, tag, postings (kind answered | confirmed | reused), first_answered_at, updated_at, revision, written_by (operator | agent) and history. The same body as GET /api/story-bank.

## `gigai scout story-bank share`

Show or set whose story bank a profile also reads.

`gigai scout story-bank share [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, profile_id, sharing}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout story-bank share --json
gigai scout story-bank share --profile profile_2 --with profile_1 --json
gigai scout story-bank share --profile profile_2 --off
```

With neither --with nor --off it only shows the setting (no write). --with makes --profile also read the OWN entries of the other profile: one hop, one way, never implicit. Profiles on one machine can be different people, so nothing is shared until this is set; --off stops it at once.

## `gigai scout story-bank show`

Show one story bank entry: the question, the full answer, who wrote it and the jobs that used it.

`gigai scout story-bank show [OPTIONS] QUESTION_ID`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, profile_id, entry}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout story-bank show cloud:gcp --json
```

QUESTION_ID is the entry's id from list. Read updated_at from here before an edit or delete with --updated-at.

## `gigai scout watchlist add`

Add a company by its Greenhouse / Lever / Ashby board (or job) URL.

`gigai scout watchlist add [OPTIONS] URL`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout watchlist add https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme
```

The URL is only parsed; no request is made until `scout sources update`. Any other host is refused. Idempotent.
